patterns.name: Block
patterns.description: Four cells in perfect balance.
patterns.tip: Step once: nothing changes.
patterns.credit: Stephen Silver’s Life Lexicon, with Dave Greene and contributors · CC BY-SA 3.0

patterns.name: Beehive
patterns.description: A hollow six-cell still life.
patterns.tip: Try placing two near one another.
patterns.credit: Stephen Silver’s Life Lexicon, with Dave Greene and contributors · CC BY-SA 3.0

patterns.name: Loaf
patterns.description: An asymmetric seven-cell still life.
patterns.tip: Use Draw to disturb its balance.
patterns.credit: Stephen Silver’s Life Lexicon, with Dave Greene and contributors · CC BY-SA 3.0

patterns.name: Boat
patterns.description: A compact five-cell still life.
patterns.tip: Place beside a glider to explore collisions.
patterns.credit: Stephen Silver’s Life Lexicon, with Dave Greene and contributors · CC BY-SA 3.0

patterns.name: Tub
patterns.description: Four cells surrounding an empty center.
patterns.tip: Each living cell has exactly two neighbors.
patterns.credit: Stephen Silver’s Life Lexicon, with Dave Greene and contributors · CC BY-SA 3.0

patterns.name: Eater gallery
patterns.description: Stable structures used to absorb moving patterns.
patterns.tip: Place a glider nearby and experiment with collisions.
patterns.credit: Golly pattern collection · original author notes preserved in the RLE file

patterns.name: Blinker
patterns.description: The simplest oscillator, repeating every two generations.
patterns.tip: Use Step to see its two orientations.
patterns.credit: Stephen Silver’s Life Lexicon, with Dave Greene and contributors · CC BY-SA 3.0

patterns.name: Toad
patterns.description: Two rows of three trade places in a period-two cycle.
patterns.tip: Step through one full cycle.
patterns.credit: Stephen Silver’s Life Lexicon, with Dave Greene and contributors · CC BY-SA 3.0

patterns.name: Beacon
patterns.description: Two blocks blink at their inner corners.
patterns.tip: Watch the two center cells disappear and return.
patterns.credit: Stephen Silver’s Life Lexicon, with Dave Greene and contributors · CC BY-SA 3.0

patterns.name: Pulsar
patterns.description: A symmetric oscillator with a three-generation cycle.
patterns.tip: Compare Step with a larger jump.
patterns.credit: Stephen Silver’s Life Lexicon, with Dave Greene and contributors · CC BY-SA 3.0

patterns.name: Pentadecathlon
patterns.description: A small pattern with a fifteen-generation rhythm.
patterns.tip: Use single steps to follow its changing shape.
patterns.credit: Stephen Silver’s Life Lexicon, with Dave Greene and contributors · CC BY-SA 3.0

patterns.name: Oscillator gallery
patterns.description: A collection of low-period oscillators on one board.
patterns.tip: Zoom in and compare their different rhythms.
patterns.credit: Golly pattern collection · original author notes preserved in the RLE file

patterns.name: Glider
patterns.description: Five cells travel diagonally across the world.
patterns.tip: After four steps, it has moved one cell diagonally.
patterns.credit: Stephen Silver’s Life Lexicon, with Dave Greene and contributors · CC BY-SA 3.0

patterns.name: Lightweight spaceship
patterns.description: A compact ship that travels horizontally.
patterns.tip: Use Step to watch its four phases.
patterns.credit: Stephen Silver’s Life Lexicon, with Dave Greene and contributors · CC BY-SA 3.0

patterns.name: Middleweight spaceship
patterns.description: A larger companion to the lightweight spaceship.
patterns.tip: Try placing ships alongside one another.
patterns.credit: Stephen Silver’s Life Lexicon, with Dave Greene and contributors · CC BY-SA 3.0

patterns.name: Heavyweight spaceship
patterns.description: The largest of the three elementary orthogonal ships.
patterns.tip: Watch it travel two cells every four generations.
patterns.credit: Stephen Silver’s Life Lexicon, with Dave Greene and contributors · CC BY-SA 3.0

patterns.name: Cordership fleet
patterns.description: Larger diagonal ships built from interacting switch engines.
patterns.tip: Try jumps of 64 to make their motion apparent.

patterns.name: R-pentomino
patterns.description: Five cells trigger a surprisingly long-lived reaction.

patterns.name: Diehard
patterns.description: Seven cells eventually disappear completely.
patterns.tip: It dies out after 130 generations.
patterns.credit: Stephen Silver’s Life Lexicon, with Dave Greene and contributors · CC BY-SA 3.0

patterns.name: Acorn
patterns.description: A seven-cell seed with thousands of generations of activity.

patterns.name: Rabbits relative
patterns.description: A tiny seed with a long and turbulent evolution.

patterns.name: Lidka predecessor
patterns.description: A compact predecessor to a long-lived methuselah.

patterns.name: Blom
patterns.description: A compact seed that develops into a much larger field.

patterns.name: Basic rakes
patterns.description: Traveling engines emit gliders as they move.

patterns.description: A growing construction fills an expanding region.

patterns.name: Glider racetrack

patterns.name: Golly ticker

patterns.name: Fermat primes
